what_happened.line: The chair said about 250 abatement applications remain outstanding after a death in the assessor's office, and the board aims to finish them before tax bills mail.
A special meeting was set for 11 A.M. Thursday, June 1, going straight into executive session with no public comment, to complete abatements.
Tentative remote meetings were scheduled for June 5, 6, 8, 13 and 15 to work through the backlog.
Two Lake Shirley property owners asked how land and building values, a fire road and seasonal use are weighed; the board said each application is reviewed individually.
The board entered executive session by roll call and said it would not return to open session; no votes were recorded.

why_it_matters: Abatement decisions change what a property owner owes, and a backlog this size can set when residents learn the outcome of their applications relative to when tax bills mail.

The June working sessions are closed or remote and the executive session takes no public comment, so owners with pending applications will mainly learn outcomes through their own notices, not through open meetings.
